docs.title: Flood events
docs.text: Upgrading a saved search to a flood event lets you add additional information and start flood investigations for each flood report included.

docs.title: Upgrade a saved search to a flood event
docs.text:
When you have your saved search ready, click on the 'Create flood event' button at the bottom of the page.

On the next page, fill in the flood event name - some information will be filled in already and you can change it as you need to.

Try and keep the name descriptive following this naming convention:

Date - Location - Flood type

Example

20-22 October 2026 - Dorchester - River

Add any other details that are currently available.

Click on 'Save flood event' when you're done.

docs.title: Adding and viewing attachments
docs.text:
On the flood event screen, click on 'Attachments'.

If a flood event already has attachments, you can view them. To add new attachments, click on the 'Upload attachments' button.

You can add images, videos and documents.

Warning

Make sure there are no identifiable people or personal data in your uploaded files.

docs.title: Create a public URL for media uploads
docs.text:
You can create a URL or QR code to share with members of the public that will let them upload media of their own. These links will work for two weeks and you can lock them sooner if you need to.

Click on the 'Generate Public Upload URL' button on the flood event page to create a sharable URL and QR code.

docs.title: Downloading data
docs.text: Download and print a PDF of a flood event, or download a CSV by using the links in the Download section.

docs.title: Flood reports
docs.text:
You can search for basic flood report details in the Risk Management app, but to see the complete report you'll be taken to the Public app.

Note

Make sure you are logged in to Public before viewing a complete flood report.

docs.title: Search for flood reports
docs.text:
Click on the 'Search for records' button on the dashboard.

Follow the guidance on saved searches and enter the details of your search.

docs.title: Viewing a basic flood report
docs.text: On the search results page, click on 'View details' next to the report you want to see more about. You'll see some basic details about the flood report.

docs.title: Viewing a complete flood report
docs.text:
On the basic flood report screen, click on the 'View the complete report' button.

You will be taken to the Public app to view the complete flood report.

Note

Make sure you are logged in to Public before viewing a complete flood report.

docs.title: Saved searches
docs.text: Create a saved search when you suspect or become aware of flooding. The reference number created from this can be shared with team members and used for monitoring.

docs.title: Creating a saved search
docs.text:
Click on the 'Search for records' button on the dashboard.

If you know the reference number of a flood event, you can use it to search. Otherwise, click on 'No' and you'll be able to search using other flood details.

You can search by:

  • Date range
  • Reports by a person's name
  • Postcode
  • Flood source type
  • Geographical area

Click on Save and any results found will be displayed in a table. You can also look at results in a list or on a map.

docs.title: What next?
docs.text: Your search is now saved. You can go on to create a flood event from your saved search if you need to.
